title: Does MCP Still Need Sessions in 2026?
description:
Stateless MCP in 60 seconds: the MCP 2026 spec changes (version 2026-07-28) removed sessions, the session ID and the initialize handshake.
Now every MCP request carries what it needs, so any server can answer it, and state lives in a ticket (a handle) your AI passes back. Told with a diner.

Read the changelog first: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog

Chapters
0:00 Why old MCP lost orders
0:11 How old MCP pinned you
0:25 New MCP: the order slip
0:37 Why it matters to you
0:47 How, why, and stateless

Status: shipped. 2026-07-28 is the current MCP protocol version (released July 28, 2026). Before it, revision 2025-11-25 started with a handshake and could give you a session ID (optional) that pinned you to one server.

The story: a diner. Your AI app is the customer; an MCP server is the waiter bringing its tools. In the old way the waiter kept your order in his head (the session), so another waiter could not take it. In the new way every request is a complete order slip (the protocol version and what the app can handle travel with it), so any waiter can take it. If a server must remember something, like a shopping basket, it hands back a ticket, an explicit handle, and your AI shows it next time. The ticket lives in your chat, so in apps that save chats it also survives a closed app or another device.

The takeaway: a server that remembers nothing is a server anyone can replace.

Sources
MCP 2026-07-28 changelog: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog
SEP-2575, Make MCP Stateless: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2575-stateless-mcp
SEP-2567, Sessionless MCP via Explicit State Handles: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2567-sessionless-mcp
Release post by the MCP lead maintainers: https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/
Current version: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning
Before (2025-11-25): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/transports

The diner is an analogy: table 12, ticket number 42, the burger and fries, and the basket's 2 items are invented examples.
Animation rendered from code. Voice by Kokoro, an open-source text-to-speech model.
